why: Sort fish and baits in descending order: the largest bait catches the largest fish first, and every fish a bait skips is too small for every smaller bait too. So one pointer walks the fish while the loop walks the baits, each bait advancing the fish pointer up to 3 times.
hints: The rules already fix the order: biggest bait first, biggest catchable fish first. What does sorting both arrays buy you?

With fish sorted descending, the remaining fish always form a suffix. A bait catches fish[i] if fish[i] > bait; if it cannot catch fish[i], it cannot catch anything after it either, and neither can smaller baits.
Sort both descending; for each bait take up to 3 fish while fish[i] > bait, advancing i. O(n log n + m log m) for the sorts, O(n + m) for the sweep.
pitfalls: The bait must be strictly smaller than the fish; equal sizes do not catch.
Each bait has a cap of 3 catches even when more fish qualify.
Once a bait fails on the largest remaining fish, no later (smaller) bait can do better; you can stop early.
